bear_case: The Iran halt is the first clean positive regime shift in two weeks, and the tape may price it more aggressively than STEP ASIDE anticipates. Markets are in Fear territory (CNN Fear & Greed ~42 as of early June) — a contrarian signal that historically precedes short-covering squeezes. Asian equities stabilized Tuesday and European benchmarks showed modest gains, reducing the overhang of forced global selling. If Trump announces a signed US-Iran MOU before Wednesday's CPI open, Brent could fall to $88–90, DXY could retreat below 100, and VIX could compress to 16–17 — removing three of five regime triggers simultaneously. Bears caught short into that scenario face a rip toward 7,500+. Invalidation: if SPX closes above 7,460 on June 9 with VIX closing below 17, STEP ASIDE reverts to HOLD immediately. If CPI prints ≤3.8% YoY with core ≤0.2% m/m on June 10, shorts cover without debate and NVDA $195–210 re-entry zone reopens.
